heads.en: Prologue on the Moralities of the Bible

headnotes.la: Sedens super thronum gloriae, est Deus gloriosus; et sublimis, regens universum, in cujus dextera est sacra Scriptura divinitus data, secundum quod dicitur Deuteronomii trigesimo tertio
headnotes.en: He that sits upon the throne of glory is the glorious God; and sublime, ruling the universe, in whose right hand is Holy Scripture divinely given, according to what is said in Deuteronomy thirty-three

headnotes.la: …bus ad aliquid significandum, sed etiam rebus per voces significatis. Et sic facta Veteris Testamenti significaverunt ea quae in Novo Testamento fiunt, sicut dicit Apostolus primo ad Corinthios decimo
headnotes.en: …fy something, but also the things signified by the words. And so the deeds of the Old Testament signified those things which are done in the New Testament, as the Apostle says in First Corinthians ten

headnotes.la: …plicem sensum praedictum, hoc tamen non est in qualibet sui parte, secundum quod dicitur in Collationibus Patrum, collatione octava. Nam alicubi habet tantum sensum litteralem sicut Deuteronomii sexto
headnotes.en: … nevertheless is not so in every part of it, according to what is said in the Conferences of the Fathers, the eighth conference. For in some places it has only the literal sense, as in Deuteronomy six

headnotes.la: etc.; in istis enim, et consimilibus, non est mysticus sensus requirendus. Alicubi vero non habet litteralem sensum proprie loquendo; verbi gratia, Judicum IX
headnotes.en: etc.; for in these, and in the like, the mystical sense is not to be sought. In some places, however, it does not have a literal sense, properly speaking; for example, Judges IX

headnotes.la: …sunt plures proprietates reales, et aliquando valde diversae; ideo una res subjective, aliquando mystice plura et diversa significat: sicut leo per proprietatem constantiae Christum significat Apoc. V
headnotes.en: …operties, and sometimes very different ones; therefore one thing as subject sometimes signifies mystically many and different things: as the lion by the property of constancy signifies Christ, Apoc. V

headnotes.la: et per voracitatem signat diabolum, primae Petri V
headnotes.en: and by its voracity signifies the devil, First Peter V

headnotes.la: …dimittam. Nam hoc faciam propter brevitatem; et quoniam sic fecerunt praecedentes expositores, et etiam Christus qui Matthaei XIII et Marci IV exponens parabolam seminantis, illud quod dicitur in fine
headnotes.en: … the sake of brevity; and because the preceding expositors did so, and also Christ, who in Matthew XIII and Mark IV, expounding the parable of the sower, left unexpounded that which is said at the end
